title: design plugin → contract v2 + ADR-063 §1/§2
goal: Migrate plugins/agent/design to the v2 result contract (result_contract:2, disposition, rc∈{0,1}, valid_verdicts, name-matched inputs) and land ADR-063 §1/§2 (inject live timeout/max_turns into the prompt so the model can emit a best-effort design before being cut off).

steps.description: Write new failing tests (TDD gate). design-v2-result-contract-test.sh asserts: (SPEC-1[change]) v2 sidecar design-verdict.json written on success path with verdict=pass disposition=complete; (SPEC-2[change]) v2 sidecar written on error path with verdict=error disposition=broken; (SPEC-3[guard]) timeout path still writes verdict=incomplete disposition=interrupted; (SPEC-4[change]) manifest result_contract==2 and valid_verdicts contains all three values; (SPEC-5[change]) plugin.sh has no hardcoded artifact paths for scope_manifest or plan. design-budget-prompt-injection-test.sh asserts: (SPEC-1[change]) prompt file contains a WALL CLOCK BUDGET and TURN BUDGET block with values sourced from _route_resolve_timeout/_route_resolve_max_turns; (SPEC-2[guard]) existing prompt instructions are unchanged for a passing run. Run both — confirm FAIL at baseline before touching implementation.

Update plugins/agent/design/manifest.yaml to declare the v2 contract. Add result_contract: 2 under provides:. Expand valid_verdicts from [incomplete] to [pass, error, incomplete]. Add config.router with timeout_s: 600 and max_turns: 45 as manifest-level defaults (the template override still wins at runtime per ADR-017; these make the budgets readable without a template). No cleanup hook added — the engine emits plugin.cleanup.absent for an absent hook (lifecycle.sh:413), which IS the recorded-not-implied contract from #1829. primary: true is already present on the design output — record that DoD item as satisfied.

Add _design_write_result helper to plugin.sh and call it on every exit path. The helper writes ${artifact_dir}/design-verdict.json with {result_contract:2, verdict, disposition, reason, data:{}} using jq -n + atomic_write (mirrors _ta_write_result from test-author). Exit paths to cover: (a) missing state_file → verdict=error disposition=broken; (b) missing plan.json → error/broken; (c) router rc=130 (SIGINT) → return 130 without writing result (abort, not a stage outcome); (d) router_timeout → verdict=incomplete disposition=interrupted (replaces bespoke #1261 sidecar write with _design_write_result call); (e) router rc>=2 → use _router_rc_classify then map to disposition (broken for most, throttled for rate-limit, unavailable for auth); (f) stray conflict → error/broken; (g) missing scope block → error/broken; (h) missing acceptance block → error/broken; (i) success → verdict=pass disposition=complete. Normalize all return 2 → return 1. Delete the bespoke design-verdict.json write block in the timeout path (now handled by _design_write_result). The success path writes result BEFORE atomic_write of design.md so the sidecar is always on disk if rc=0.

Replace hardcoded artifact path construction with ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS lookups. In design_stage_run: delete 'local scope_manifest="$state_dir/scope-manifest.md"' and 'local plan_json_path="$artifacts_dir/plan.json"'; instead read them as jq .inputs.scope_manifest and .inputs.plan from "$ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS" (when ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS is set and the file exists), falling back to the old path construction when the index is absent (defensive: the flag may not be on in all test harnesses). For the optional 'design' input (prior design body): read .inputs.design from the index when present and non-empty, and use it as the prior-design content instead of calling _design_read_prior_design — this replaces both Tier 1 (intra-cycle feedback) and Tier 2 (restored artifact) lookup because the engine's input-resolve.sh already consolidates those tiers when writing the index. Keep _design_read_prior_design as a private fallback callable when the index key is absent, so existing test fixtures that set ZBUILD_CYCLE_FEEDBACK_DIR directly keep working.

Add ADR-063 §1/§2 budget guidance injection (mirrors plan plugin's _plan_budget_guidance/_plan_wallclock_guidance). Add two private helpers: _design_budget_guidance <max_turns> (emits a TURN BUDGET block when max_turns>0) and _design_wallclock_guidance <timeout_s> <elapsed_s> (emits a WALL CLOCK BUDGET block with 70% target stop time). In _design_stage_run_inner, after route.sh is sourced, call _route_resolve_max_turns (with ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE=design) and _route_resolve_timeout to get the live values, then append the budget blocks to the prompt file BEFORE the prompt-override append (so operator overlay appears last, per ADR-032). Also append a 'best-effort' instruction: if the model has not finished all sections when the budget nears, it must name the unfinished sections rather than silently omitting them — this is the §2 requirement that a partial design is safer than a silent one, gated by the §3/§4 check in design-gate.

Run npm test (full suite). Verify the two new tests from step-1 pass. Verify the existing design unit tests (design-router-timeout-reiter-test.sh, design-timeout-exhaustion-halt-1261-test.sh, design-acceptance-block-test.sh, design-persona-framing-test.sh) still pass — they are guards. If any existing test fails because it inspects the sidecar JSON shape, update the fixture to the v2 shape (result_contract:2, disposition field present). Check coverage floor is still met (bash scripts/check-coverage.sh). Record the red-step assertion and how it failed at baseline in the PR body.

notes:
GAPS AND ASSUMPTIONS:

1. Input resolution fallback: Step-4 keeps _design_read_prior_design as a fallback when ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS is absent. If the prior-output-reader ADR-050 Tier-1/Tier-2 seam is fully superseded by input-resolve.sh in a live dispatch, the fallback is dead code. But existing unit tests that inject ZBUILD_CYCLE_FEEDBACK_DIR without going through lifecycle.sh will break if the fallback is removed entirely. Safest approach: read from index first, fall back to the tier-1/tier-2 reader. If product expectation is clean deletion, the implementation agent should also update the test fixtures.

2. Router budgets key name: The manifest uses config.router.timeout_s and config.router.max_turns per _route_resolve_knob. The issue references #1816 'router budgets'. The plan plugin uses config.router.{retries, retry_on_exhaustion} — these are additive. The defaults I propose (timeout_s:600, max_turns:45) are conservative; the template override (600s, max_turns:0) still wins at runtime. The implementation agent should confirm the exact knob names by checking _route_resolve_knob's 4th arg (the manifest key).

3. design_result declared output: The v2 sidecar design-verdict.json is read by _verdict_read_stage_sidecar generically — it is NOT a declared output in the manifest and should not be. Do not add it as an output entry. The existing mechanism already reads it.

4. rc=130 SIGINT: The issue says rc ∈ {0,1}; SIGINT (rc=130) is a hard abort, not a stage outcome. Propagating rc=130 without writing a result is correct — the engine treats an aborted dispatch differently from a failed one. No change needed for the SIGINT arm except removing return 2 on other paths.

5. ADR-063 §3/§4: The issue says §3/§4 (the design-gate check that refuses a partial design) is out of scope for plugin.sh — it belongs in design-gate. This plan deliberately scopes only §1/§2 (prompt injection) to the design plugin.

6. 'did_not_finish' vocabulary: The cycle-orchestrator already reads disposition=interrupted from the blob (cycle-orchestrator.sh:2335). The test fixture (design-timeout-exhaustion-halt-1261-test.sh) already uses this vocabulary. No orchestrator changes needed.

7. Cleanup hook: The issue says 'if it has nothing to free, the hook is absent and that is recorded, not implied.' The manifest has no cleanup hook today; lifecycle.sh already emits plugin.cleanup.absent (rc=0). No manifest change needed for cleanup.

8. Step-6 has estimated_lines:0 because it is a verification step, not a code-writing step. The CLAUDE.md 'state the red step' requirement means the PR body (not a file in scope) records the failing assertion.

9. WIRING: The wiring for this migration is the manifest itself (plugins/agent/design/manifest.yaml) — its result_contract:2 declaration gates the engine's strict v2 reading. The implementation files (plugin.sh + tests) are the implementation.
